title: fix(security): `$expand` no longer discloses records the caller is 403'd from — the #2850 expand waiver is removed (#7626)
body:
Fixes #7626.

## Premise verification (done before implementing)

The issue's mechanism was re-derived against `origin/main` @ `cc3555e` and **holds**, with one correction and one addition:

| Issue says | Measured on `origin/main` |
|---|---|
| `:1206` `expandSkipCrud = … && !secMeta.isPrivate` | ✅ confirmed (line drift aside) |
| `:4314` `isPrivate: obj?.access?.default === 'private'` | ✅ confirmed — a different axis from `sharingModel` |
| "`:1216` and `:1274` — the CRUD check and the effective-scope application" | ⚠️ **corrected**: `:1216` is the `requiredPermissions` AND-gate and `:1274` is the CRUD check. The effective-scope stash (step 2.6) is **not** guarded by `expandSkipCrud` — see the OWD mechanism below, which is a consequence of the skipped CRUD check rather than a second guard |
| "`access` is `null` in the built artifact, so the waiver fires for every referenced object" | ✅ confirmed — `showcase_contact` declares `sharingModel: 'private'` and no `access` block |

**How the OWD scope actually falls.** Step 2.6 stashes `sc.__readScope = getEffectiveScope('read', …)`, and `getEffectiveScope` returns `'org'` — the *widest* depth — when **no** permission set grants the operation. Its own comment says that is safe because "the caller denies separately, so the value is unused". The waiver is precisely what stopped the caller being denied, so the skipped CRUD check also handed plugin-sharing an org-wide read depth and dissolved the owner filter. One skip, both gates.

Reproduced end-to-end on the real showcase app (see "Verified red, then green" below): a `contributor`-only session is `403` on `GET /data/showcase_contact/:id` and receives that same contact fully materialised — `email` included — through `?$expand=contact`, `?expand=contact` and the body `expand` door alike.

## Why #2850 added the waiver, and why removing it is the right shape

I read #2850 and its PR #2961 before choosing. **#2850's subject was not the waiver.** The defect was that `expandRelatedRecords` called `driver.find` directly, so a referenced object's RLS/FLS never ran at all. PR #2961 fixed that by routing the sub-read through `this.find` tagged `__expandRead` — **that half is correct and is kept untouched.** The waiver was a *concession* bolted onto it, justified in the PR as:

> a PUBLIC referenced object … is already broadly readable via the `'*'` wildcard grant, so applying that gate to an expansion would over-block common status/owner lookups without adding protection.

Both halves of that premise fail:

1. **Wrong axis.** `access.default` (ADR-0066 D2 — whether a `'*'` wildcard *covers* the object) is not the `sharingModel` OWD that scopes an object's *rows*. Nearly every object leaves `access` unset, so nearly every object read as "public".
2. **The premise was never checked.** The condition asks nothing about the caller's grants. #2850's own unit pin waives the gate for a permission set with `objects: {}` — a caller holding *literally nothing*. Where the premise is true the waiver is **inert** (the CRUD gate would pass anyway); its only non-vacuous effect is on callers the gate meant to refuse. A waiver that only fires when its own justification is false is not protecting a legitimate behaviour.

So the card's option (a) — re-key on `sharingModel` — was rejected on measurement: it closes the `showcase_contact` case but leaves a `public_read` object with no grant fully disclosed through the same door. Option (b), removing the waiver, is what landed.

**Nothing over-blocks.** `expandRelatedRecords` already wraps the sub-read in a `try/catch` whose documented behaviour is "graceful degradation: if expand fails, keep original IDs". A caller who cannot read the referenced object now gets the bare FK id it already had — the parent read still returns 200. This is the exact behaviour #2961 described for private objects; it is now uniform.

`__expandRead` itself stays. It is not left unenforced: the storage and comment access hooks strip it as a privileged widening input, and `core`'s operation-private-keys list is what keeps it unforgeable from the wire.

## Changes

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` — **the fix.** `expandSkipCrud` deleted; the `requiredPermissions` AND-gate (step 1.5) and the CRUD check (step 2) now run for every referenced object. The replacing comment records the two failed premises and the OWD mechanism.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-expand-crud-gate.dogfood.test.ts` — **new**, the regression proof (below).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.test.ts` — the `#2850` unit pins re-aimed: the "WAIVES the CRUD gate for a PUBLIC referenced object" case is inverted (it encoded the hole), and a second case pins that the `requiredPermissions` gate is not waived either. Their header now says outright that this shape cannot be the regression story.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/operation-private-keys.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` + three test files — comment-only. Each stated "`__expandRead` waives the object-level CRUD gate" as fact; that is now false and would mislead the next reader.
- `.changeset/expand-crud-gate-cross-persona-disclosure.md` — user-visible security fix, `@objectstack/plugin-security` patch. Only that package changes behaviour; the others are comments, so they are deliberately not bumped.

## The regression test is end-to-end and two-persona

`showcase-expand-crud-gate.dogfood.test.ts` boots the real showcase app through the in-process HTTP stack with **two live sessions** and compares outcomes. Deliberately **not** a re-tagged `__expandRead` unit assertion — that shape is what stayed green for the whole life of this disclosure, and the file's header says so.

The persona is the app's own `showcase_contributor` set, unmodified: it names `showcase_invoice` and does not name `showcase_contact`, and neither does the `showcase_member_default` baseline. That absence *is* the fixture. It boots its own stack rather than the shared showcase, because `shared-showcase.ts` hands its baseline an explicit `showcase_contact` read grant for an unrelated fixture.

10 assertions:

- the persona is `403` on the contact directly, by id **and** by list (the premise);
- the persona can read the parent invoice it owns (so expand is reachable at all);
- **admin sees the contact materialised** vs **the denied persona does not**, through all three doors — query-string `$expand` on the list route, `expand` on the by-id route, and the body `expand` on `POST …/query`. The withheld assertion is on the raw response text (`not.toContain` the contact's email), so a partially-materialised record cannot slip through, plus a structural check that the FK degraded to the bare id;
- **over-correction guard 1**: the persona's foreign-invoice query still returns **200 with 0 rows** — RLS filters, it does not refuse — and its own row is still returned by the same door;
- **over-correction guard 2**: a lookup the persona *does* hold a grant on (`showcase_account`) still expands to a full record.

The body-door case includes `id` in the nested `fields` on purpose — without it the expansion is a silent no-op (#7537, the functional twin of this seam) and the assertion would pass for the wrong reason.

## Verified red, then green

The dogfood suite resolves `@objectstack/plugin-security` from `dist`, so the check was run against real builds, not edited source:

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| waiver **restored**, package rebuilt | **3 failed** — the contributor receives the full contact (`"email":"expand-secret-contact@verify.test"`) through all three doors; the two over-correction guards pass on both sides |
| waiver **removed**, package rebuilt | **10 passed** |

## Gates run locally

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm build` (turbo, 71 tasks) | ✅ |
| `@objectstack/plugin-security` (the sibling-plane pin) | ✅ 953 passed / 46 files |
| `@objectstack/dogfood` — **full** suite | ✅ 573 passed, 3 skipped / 90 files |
| `@objectstack/objectql` | ✅ 3187 passed |
| `@objectstack/rest` | ✅ 1397 passed |
| `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` | ✅ 1062 passed |
| `@objectstack/core` | ✅ 764 passed |
| `@objectstack/service-storage` | ✅ 352 passed |
| `@objectstack/plugin-audit` | ✅ 201 passed |
| `typecheck` (all touched packages + dogfood) | ✅ |
| `eslint --no-inline-config` (changed files) | ✅ |
| `check:authz-resolver`, `check:verify-stand-in`, `check:query-options-erasure` | ✅ |

The full `lint.yml` farm was not enumerated locally — CI runs it once.

## Notes

- The new dogfood file deliberately carries **no** `@proof:` tag. ADR-0054 proofs gate the `live` status of an *authorable property*; this one gates none, and a tag would only add an unregistered orphan to `proof-registry.mts`.
- #7537 (the functional half of the same seam — `expand` is a silent no-op when nested `fields` omits `id`) is untouched here: different file, `domain:engine-core`. This PR's body-door test works *around* it rather than fixing it, and will keep passing either way.
